_comment: t 是距开场的秒数。utterance 在所有模式下播放；scripted 只在 MODE=scripted 下播放（代替真实 agent 的输出，供前端开发用）。

items.speaker: s1
items.text: Okay, we have about five minutes to lock an idea. Education track. What have we got?

items.speaker: s3
items.text: What about an AI study buddy that turns your lecture recordings into flashcards automatically?

items.speaker: s2
items.text: Oh I like that. I could make the flashcards look really nice, like a swipe deck.

items.speaker: s4
items.text: Has anyone done that already? It sounds familiar.

items.speaker: s3
items.text: Not sure. Probably not exactly this.

items.title: This space is crowded
items.say: Flashcards from recordings already exist, but none of these tools work live during the lecture.
items.body: Quizlet Q-Chat, Anki add-ons and NotebookLM already turn notes and recordings into flashcards. None of them work live during the lecture.

items.speaker: s1
items.text: Hmm, so the flashcard part is taken. What if it's live, during the lecture?

items.speaker: s2
items.text: Speaking of lectures, did you see the new lecture hall? The screens are huge, we should film the video there.

items.speaker: s3
items.text: Yeah and the coffee place next to it is great, we could go after this.

items.speaker: s2
items.text: They have that oat flat white. Honestly the best on campus.

items.title: One minute in, no idea chosen yet
items.body: About four minutes are left and there is one candidate idea: a live lecture companion. Innovation is 30% of the score.
items.say: Quick check, we have about four minutes left. Do we want to go deeper on the live lecture idea, or hear one more option?

items.speaker: s1
items.text: Right, back to it. Live lecture companion. Students learn eighty percent better with spaced repetition, so we just build that in.

items.speaker: s3
items.text: Sure, eighty percent, that's a great number for the video.

items.title: The 80% figure isn't established
items.say: That eighty percent figure isn't established. The gains are real, but they vary a lot by study.
items.body: Spaced repetition reliably improves long-term retention, but effect sizes vary a lot by study and material. A single '80% better' number isn't supported. Safer wording: 'well-evidenced gains in retention'.

items.speaker: s4
items.text: Fine, we'll soften the number. So are we all happy with the live companion?

items.speaker: s2
items.text: Yes, love it.

items.speaker: s3
items.text: Agreed.

items.speaker: s1
items.text: Great, sounds good to everyone. Let's go with it.

items.title: Nobody has named a risk yet
items.body: Everyone agreed in under ten seconds. Open question: live transcription in a noisy lecture hall is the hardest part, and it is the whole demo.
items.say: Before you lock it in, what happens to the demo if live transcription fails in a noisy room?

items.speaker: s4
items.text: That's fair. We could pre-record a lecture clip as a fallback.

items.speaker: s1
items.text: Hey Scout, is there an open dataset of lecture recordings we could use?

items.title: Lecture recordings you can use
items.body: MIT OpenCourseWare publishes full lecture videos under a Creative Commons licence. Good enough for a pre-recorded fallback clip.
items.say: MIT OpenCourseWare has full lectures under Creative Commons. Want me to pull one for the fallback clip?

items.speaker: s3
items.text: Perfect. I'll take the transcription pipeline.

items.speaker: s2
items.text: I'll do the interface and the video.

items.speaker: s4
items.text: I'll set up the server and the fallback recording.

items.speaker: s1
items.text: And I'll write the script and keep us on the judging criteria. Done.
